checks.interruption: An installed CLI run was killed with SIGKILL after a published checkpoint. The same manifest resumed through installed MCP; applied and skipped counts matched the checkpoint, item IDs and event sequences remained unique, CLI and MCP status agreed, and a second replay left ledger bytes unchanged.
checks.paired_writers: Two installed CLI put processes with distinct declared actor IDs, target expected_version=0 and direct dependency p1=1 were released from a shell barrier. Both exited successfully without caller retries; three event sequences, actor attribution, dependency versions and CLI/MCP status were checked.

limits: The shell barrier does not prove the two CLI processes read the same ledger revision or exercised an internal retry. A separate development unit test forces that collision, but this wheel smoke does not.
The SIGKILL followed a durable checkpoint; it does not exercise interruption inside an atomic replacement or host power loss.
Distinct actor labels on local CLI processes do not prove two model agents worked concurrently.
The wheel is a local uncommitted build artifact. All case contents and signatures are synthetic. No human normative approval, field effect, or controlled model comparison is shown.
